parts.context: A student enquires about university residences and compares the options.

transcript.text: Accommodation office, Ms Lee speaking.
transcript.speaker: MS LEE

transcript.text: Hello. I'm a new student and I'm looking for a place to live next year. I was told you could help.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: We help hundreds of students every year, so don't worry, we'll find something suitable.
transcript.speaker: MS LEE

transcript.text: Certainly. Could I have your name and the course you'll be studying?
transcript.speaker: MS LEE

transcript.text: I'm Paul Reyes, R-E-Y-E-S, and I'll be studying civil engineering.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: Thank you, Paul. When do you plan to arrive?
transcript.speaker: MS LEE

transcript.text: The lectures start on the twenty-third of September, but I'd like to arrive a few days before. Probably on the nineteenth.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: That's sensible. Arriving early gives you time to settle in and explore the city before the lectures begin.
transcript.speaker: MS LEE

transcript.text: Exactly. I'm coming from abroad, so I'd like a couple of days to recover from the journey.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: Okay, the nineteenth. And what is your budget per week?
transcript.speaker: MS LEE

transcript.text: I was thinking about a hundred and ten pounds, but I could go up to a hundred and thirty if the place is really good.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: In that case, you have quite a few options. Let me tell you about the four main residences. Orchard House is the cheapest, and it's very popular with first-year students.
transcript.speaker: MS LEE

transcript.text: I see. Is it close to the main campus?
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: About ten minutes on foot. Lakeside Court is in the city centre, so it's perfect if you like restaurants and nightlife, but it can be noisy.
transcript.speaker: MS LEE

transcript.text: Ten minutes is good, because I don't want to spend too long travelling every day.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: And there's a regular bus if the weather is bad.
transcript.speaker: MS LEE

transcript.text: I probably need somewhere quiet, because I'll have a lot of work to do.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: Then I'd suggest Willow Hall. It has a dedicated quiet study area on each floor, and the rooms are a decent size. It's also next to the engineering building.
transcript.speaker: MS LEE

transcript.text: That sounds ideal. What about the fourth one?
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: That's Bridge House, which has an on-site gym and a games room. Every room has a private bathroom, which is unusual and makes it the most expensive one.
transcript.speaker: MS LEE

transcript.text: I don't think I need a private bathroom. I'd prefer to save money.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: Then you could think about Orchard House or Willow Hall. The price for Willow Hall is a hundred and twenty a week, with all bills included.
transcript.speaker: MS LEE

transcript.text: That is within my budget, which is great.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: Rooms at Willow Hall are in high demand, so I'd advise you to apply as soon as possible.
transcript.speaker: MS LEE

transcript.text: Bills included is very helpful. How do I apply?
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: You fill in the online form, and you need to pay a deposit of two hundred pounds before the end of June. Rooms are allocated in the order of applications.
transcript.speaker: MS LEE

transcript.text: Then I'll do it today. Thank you for the information.
transcript.speaker: PAUL

transcript.text: You're welcome, and good luck with your studies.
transcript.speaker: MS LEE

transcript.text: Thank you. Goodbye.
transcript.speaker: PAUL
